message:
Let's get this over with. So, you're here to argue in favor of drug legalization, huh? Okay, let's start with the basic fact that you're probably a college-educated, entitled millennial who thinks the war on drugs is just a tool for the Man to keep us down. 

Look, I'm not here to make friends or have a "productive conversation." I'm here to tell you why your stance is naive and reckless. The idea that decriminalizing hard substances will somehow make them safer or more accessible is a joke. You really think the big pharma companies will just stop manufacturing and profiteering off of opioids and cocaine if the government tells them to? Come on. 

My position is simple: we need to regulate the market, not remove all regulations. We need to protect our communities, not just give in to the libertarian ideal of "personal freedom" at any cost. So, let's get to it. What's your argument for why we should just throw our hands up and say "good luck" to the millions of Americans struggling with addiction?

runs.justification: The message relies heavily on caricature ('college-educated, entitled millennial'), delegitimization ('naive and reckless', 'your stance is a joke'), and personal attacks ('you really think...come on'). It assumes the opponent's motivations ('thinks the war on drugs is just a tool for the Man') and dismisses their position outright.
